Every edge below was machine-drafted, span-exact and passed the B6 rule layer,
then labelled independently by two annotators and reconciled under D-30.
The two edges they both rejected are gone; what remains is four per graph,
exactly MIN_EDGES. Agreement figures are in reports/adjudication_kappa_test.md
and the attestation is signed separately in review_receipt.json.

Two of the four test queries carry no graph. test-cpi-effects is not drafted. The feasibility audit's partner count is a co-occurrence count, and reading the passages shows this corpus treats Indian headline CPI as an effect of the oil shock rather than a cause, so an effects graph rooted at CPI reaches one or two edges, not MIN_EDGES.
`test-cpi-why` is excluded by D-27.

## `test-fpi-why`

Anchor `FPI_FLOWS` down, cutoff 2026-04-20, 4 edges.

| edge | claim | strength | hop | passage | span |
|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| `tw1` | FPI_FLOWS -> INR_USD (up) | direct | 1 | `businessline-469aabd081e5b5594ab2#p4` | the rupee is under pressure as exporter payments are not materialising, dollar outflows on account of FPI selling in domestic equity markets continuing |
| `tw3` | INR_USD -> IMPORT_BILL (up) | conditional | 2 | `economic_times-6a4582bc53bfe30b98f6#p5` | A sustained depreciation in the rupee would directly inflate the import bill |
| `tw4` | INR_USD -> CURRENT_ACCOUNT_DEFICIT (up) | conditional | 2 | `economic_times-6a4582bc53bfe30b98f6#p5` | A sustained depreciation in the rupee would directly inflate the import bill, widen both the current account deficit |
| `tw5` | INR_USD -> FISCAL_DEFICIT (up) | conditional | 2 | `economic_times-6a4582bc53bfe30b98f6#p5` | A sustained depreciation in the rupee would directly inflate the import bill, widen both the current account deficit and fiscal deficit |

- **`tw1`** - Three causes are listed together and FPI selling is one of them. A reviewer must decide whether 'on account of' attributes the pressure to FPI selling directly or only lists it alongside two others.
- **`tw3`** - Hypothetical ('would'), so drafted conditional. Do not upgrade it.
- **`tw4`** - Same sentence as tw3 and tw5. One span, three destinations: check that each destination's move is stated, not just listed.
- **`tw5`** - 'widen both the current account deficit and fiscal deficit' - the verb is shared. A reviewer may read the fiscal leg as weaker than the current-account leg.
